metadata.name: R21 · level-2 prior: walk straight — vx → 0.3 m/s, yaw rate → 0, prior-only (HK on = a spin)
metadata.description: Phase 1e of the intent boundary (design doc §16.4): the same module code one level up. The 'motors' are the three twist commands (vx, vy, vyaw) to Pollen's walking policy, the 'senses' are the body's own velocity from contact odometry and the gyro, normalised by the trained command ranges (0.4, 0.3, 1.0). Identification by held twist pulses (babble_hold 75 ticks = 1.5 s, scale 0.8 of range — above the walker's ~0.25 m/s standing regime), one motor at a time, alternating sign. Judged on the identified A: the velocity rows against the commands must be positive on the diagonal and dominant, per axis, against the walker's measured response (§16.2). No prior, no controller learning: identification only.
scaffolds_active: alpha_walking.onnx drives the joints throughout — the level-2 body; alpha_stand rescues falls

description: R21 (level-2 prior: walk straight — vx → 0.3 m/s, yaw rate → 0, learned through the identified A), from a1v2_r20_l2_ident.json: The first level-2 control (design doc §16.5): a state prior on the sensed forward velocity (slot 0, target 0.75 of the 0.4 m/s range = 0.3 m/s) and on the yaw rate (slot 6, target 0), with the controller learning (ctrl_lr 0.1) through the A that R20 identified. Babble 600 s, then the prior drives. Judged on forward speed and heading drift over the control phase against the walker under a constant forward command, which drifts 5-8 deg/s by itself. MEASURED (2026-09-03): with ctrl_lr 0.1 the homeokinetic term saturates the yaw command on its own efference copy (C's yaw row: yaw act -57) and the body spins at 7 deg/s, dither or not; with ctrl_lr 0 (this file) the prior alone walks straight: 0.00 deg/s drift, straightness 0.90, 0.21 m/s, 0 falls over 800 s.
